items.item_text: California Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW)

Equipped with the skills, knowledge, and experience to address death, dying, and bereavement issues

The Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) provides comprehensive, evidence-based clinical social work services to patients and families experiencing complex medical, behavioral health, and psychosocial needs. This position will primarily support pediatric patients and their families within UC Davis Children’s Hospital. Using advanced clinical assessment and judgment, the LCSW develops patient-centered interventions that consider each patient’s diagnosis, functioning, support system, living environment, and social determinants of health.
40% - Uses Clinical Social Work Process and Practice

Clinical services include biopsychosocial assessment, crisis intervention, psychiatric diagnostic evaluation informed by current DSM guidelines, suicide risk assessment and safety planning, supportive and grief counseling, harm reduction, mandated reporting, and support for individuals impacted by violence, abuse, neglect, or human trafficking. The LCSW also assists with complex needs such as identifying unknown patients, locating next of kin, and connecting patients and families with essential community resources.
20% - Coordination and Collaboration

Working collaboratively with the interdisciplinary treatment team, the LCSW provides therapeutic intervention, advocacy, education, and care coordination to promote patient well-being, continuity of care, and safe transitions throughout the healthcare system. The position is part of Clinical Social Services’ 24-hour, seven-day-a-week care model, supporting continuous access to clinical social work services.
